note: Order of the guided run (/grammatik/lauf) and of every topic list sorted by level (src/lib/lehrplan.js). This is a teaching decision, not a derived sort: within a level, what later topics build on comes first. English order (2026-10-29, grammar-structure run): A1 starts with be, nouns and articles, then the present simple and questions, then the small everyday structures; A2 adds the present continuous and the past simple before quantifiers, comparison and modals; B1 is built round the present perfect, narrative tenses and the future, then conditionals, verb patterns, relative clauses, the passive and reported speech; B2 and C1 follow the same idea (the forms first, the linkers and refinements later). Only topics listed here are part of the run (core). Topics left out are extra practice (reference and word-formation topics: wortarten, komposita, wortbildung-nomen): they keep their page and their place in the index, but they do not lengthen the run. Each topic must be listed under its own `level`. Drafts ("status": "entwurf") only count once they are reviewed. An entry "id:A2" would be the A2 part of a topic that teaches two levels on one page (exercise titles "A2: …"); no English topic does this at the moment.
